note: A starting point, not a finished list. Shown at most once per check-in, and a check-in without one is complete (FR-008). Selection criteria are recorded in research.md R6: observational rather than hortatory, nothing to exhort, congratulate, or count.
quotes: The evening arrived the same way it always does, one minute after another.
Somewhere a porch light is on and no one is thinking about it.
A kettle takes about as long to boil as it takes to sit down.
The window is either open or it isn't.
Most rooms are quieter after nine than anyone plans for.
A wall holds the heat of the afternoon a little longer than the air does.
Tomorrow's weather is already decided somewhere over the ocean.
The last hour of the day looks a lot like the first.
A doormat is generally damper than the step in front of it.
A glass of water left on a table slowly comes to room temperature.
The moon does not care what day of the week it is.
A chair holds its shape whether or not someone is sitting in it.
The hum of a refrigerator is easier to hear at night.
Streetlights come on before anyone asks them to.
The floor creaks in the same spot every time someone crosses the hallway.
Somewhere it is already tomorrow.
The dark takes about the same time to arrive each night this month.
A stack of folded towels stays exactly as tall as it was left.
Rain sounds different on a roof than on a window.
The clock on the wall keeps its own pace, unbothered.
A house settles a little every evening as it cools.
Most evenings end quietly, without anyone noticing the exact moment.
The last bus of the evening keeps its schedule whether or not anyone boards.
A gate settles into its latch under its own weight.
